name: Deterministic diagnostic replay
summary: A production failure becomes actionable when its build, content, platform, seed, configuration, inputs, authoritative events, and stop point can be replayed or its first divergence identified.
player_action: A tester or player encounters a crash, hitch, state disagreement, inaccessible cue, or progression defect.
system_response: The diagnostic path captures a bounded reproduction packet and compares replayed checkpoints until it reproduces the failure or names the earliest unsupported difference.

conflicts_with: claims of reproduction without matching environment

failure_modes: The replay uses a different build or configuration without disclosing it.
Input logs omit asynchronous state that controlled the failure.
The packet captures private data unrelated to reproduction.
A non-reproduced report is silently treated as disproven.
accessibility: Capture active accessibility configuration because it can alter input and presentation paths.
Allow local export and readable consent before transmitting diagnostic evidence.

smallest_playable_test.setup: Inject one deterministic crash, one frame hitch, one save disagreement, and one dropped accessibility cue into an instrumented arena, then reproduce each from a bounded packet on a second machine.
smallest_playable_test.retain_if: Each injected failure reproduces or stops at a named external dependency without collecting unrelated data.
smallest_playable_test.revise_if: The packet locates divergence but remains too large or platform-specific for routine use.
smallest_playable_test.reject_if: A matching packet reports success while replayed authoritative state differs or diagnostics leak undeclared data.

notes: Provisional until a repository-owned executable replay reproduces injected failures across at least two environments.
